# LITs with `tags` `behavioral-integration`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds what the Anthology of the SOTA does not: reading whose subject no anthology topic can hold. The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Behavioral integration** — how an organism's many control systems come to act as one — action selection and competition between systems (habitual and goal-directed, automatic and willed), hierarchical and feedback control, intertemporal conflict and self-control, and evidence accumulation to a decision. One of four unities kept apart (ADR-024).

| [LIT-565](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-565.md) | The Time Course of Perceptual Choice: The Leaky, Competing Accumulator Model | Usher & McClelland (2001), Psychological Review 108(3):550–592. Perceptual choice as gradual, stochastic accumulation in one unit per alternative, with leakage and lateral inhibition between units and a threshold at zero. For two choices the linearised difference is an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process with net leak K = k − β; K = 0 recovers the classical diffusion model, and K ≠ 0 bounds asymptotic accuracy. In the linear two-choice case the difference between accumulators is an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process with net leak K = k − β, so the classical diffusion model is the special case K = 0 and accuracy given unlimited time is bounded whenever K ≠ 0. Its evidence for leakage over drift variance is a modest likelihood advantage on 3 participants (combined ratio about 62 to 1, 7 of 9 curves), and the authors concede that a diffusion model with drift variance, starting-point variance and decision boundaries is hard to tell apart from it. |

The pure drift diffusion model is the continuum limit of the SPRT, so it is the fastest for a given accuracy and the most accurate for a given time. Of six models, all but the race model reduce to it in some parameter range: the Usher–McClelland mutual inhibition model when leak equals inhibition and both are large, the feedforward inhibition model when its inhibitory and excitatory weights are equal. | [LIT-577](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-577.md) | Sophisticated Inference | Friston, Da Costa, Hafner, Hesp & Parr (2021; arXiv 2020), Neural Computation 33(3):713–763. Ordinary active inference scores a fixed set of policies by expected free energy (risk plus ambiguity). Sophisticated inference instead evaluates the expected free energy of the next action recursively, averaging over the beliefs the agent would hold after each plausible outcome and action, which amounts to a tree search over belief states pruned below a probability of 1/16. In simulations it plans past short-term costs: a rat visits a mildly aversive cue, and a horizon of four escapes a local minimum in a maze. It recovers Bayes-adaptive RL in the zero-temperature limit. | Active — read in full 2026-10-03 ([NOTE-454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-454.md)), from the arXiv preprint, whose displayed equations did not survive text extraction. Worth reading as the active-inference planning scheme the record's free-energy holdings otherwise lack: expected free energy evaluated recursively over future belief states, a deep tree search pruned by probability, with the Bellman equation as its formal analogue. The evidence is small simulations (a T-maze rat and an 8 × 8 grid). Flagged anthology-candidate: it is a planning algorithm, compared with reinforcement learning, and the anthology's agents-and-environments topic may hold it. |

| [LIT-580](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-580.md) | Uncertainty-based competition between prefrontal and dorsolateral striatal systems for behavioral control | Daw, Niv & Dayan (2005), Nature Neuroscience 8(12):1704-1711. Habitual and goal-directed control are model-free ("caching") and model-based ("tree-search") reinforcement learners in dorsolateral striatum and prefrontal cortex. Behaviour follows whichever controller's value estimate is less uncertain under approximate Bayesian versions of each. Simulations reproduce the devaluation data: over-training yields devaluation-insensitive habit, except for actions near reward or in tasks with more actions and outcomes. Both controllers serve the same ends; neither is the "irrational" one. | Active — read in full 2026-10-03 ([NOTE-459](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-459.md)), supplementary methods not read. Worth reading as the founding statement of model-based versus model-free control as two brain systems, and of arbitration between them by relative uncertainty. Goal-directed (devaluation-sensitive) behaviour is a prefrontal "tree-search" controller, statistically efficient but noisy to compute. Habit is a dorsolateral-striatal "caching" controller, cheap but data-hungry and blind to revaluation. Each controls behaviour when its value estimate is the more certain, which reproduces why over-training produces habits unless the task is complex or the action near the reward. Both controllers pursue "identical rational ends": a rejection of the impulsive-limbic-versus-rational-prefrontal picture. |

Hierarchical RL groups actions into reusable "options" with their own policies, subgoals and pseudo-reward. That eases the scaling problem by cutting the number of decisions to explore and learn. The paper builds an actor-critic version and maps option identifiers to DLPFC, option-specific policies to dorsolateral striatum, and option-specific values and option-length prediction errors to OFC. Unsuitable options produce negative transfer, so how useful options are discovered is the central open problem. | Active — read in full 2026-10-03 ([NOTE-451](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-451.md)), from the PubMed Central author manuscript; the online appendix with the equations was not read. Worth reading as the bridge between hierarchical reinforcement learning (temporally abstract "options") and the psychology and neuroscience of hierarchically organized behaviour. Options ease the scaling problem of RL by shrinking search and learning to a few decision points. An actor-critic version maps option identifiers to dorsolateral PFC, option-specific policies to dorsolateral striatum, and option-specific values and extended prediction errors to orbitofrontal cortex. The problem it puts first is option discovery: the wrong options cause negative transfer, as in human problem solving. |

The account integrates conflict monitoring, effort costs and the override of defaults (exploration, foraging, patience). | Active — read in full 2026-10-03 ([NOTE-446](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-446.md)), from the PubMed Central author manuscript. Worth reading as the standard statement that cognitive control is allocated by a cost-benefit decision. The "expected value of control" (EVC) of a control signal, which has an identity (which task) and an intensity (how much), is its expected payoff minus an intrinsic cost that rises with intensity. Dorsal anterior cingulate cortex is proposed to monitor and to specify the EVC-maximizing signal, which lateral PFC and subcortical structures then implement. It is a review and synthesis: the model is stated, not fitted, and the authors say the ingredients are not new. |
| [LIT-586](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-586.md) | Précis of Breakdown of Will | Ainslie (2005), Behavioral and Brain Sciences 28(5), the précis of Breakdown of Will (2001). People and other animals discount delayed rewards hyperbolically, so preferences reverse as a smaller, sooner reward comes near, and a person becomes a population of reward-seeking "interests" that must forestall one another. Willpower is the bundling of future choices by treating the present one as a precedent: an intertemporal repeated prisoner's dilemma, not an organ or a top-down ego. The same recursion predicts the will's costs: legalism, circumscribed "lapse districts", motivated blindness to lapses, and rules that favour countable goals over subtle ones. | Active — read in full 2026-10-03 ([NOTE-443](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-443.md)), as the substitute for the 2001 book ([LIT-583](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-583.md)), which the owner suggested and which the précis follows chapter by chapter. Worth reading as the shortest complete statement of picoeconomics in Ainslie's own words. Hyperbolic discounting makes preference reverse as a smaller, sooner reward draws near, so a person behaves like a population of "interests" that bargain across time. Will is not a faculty above them but a recursive self-prediction: treating each choice as a precedent "bundles" future rewards, an intertemporal repeated prisoner's dilemma in which "credibility is power". The same mechanism predicts the will's side effects: legalism, "lapse districts", motivated misperception and compulsive over-control. |
| [LIT-588](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-588.md) | A theoretical model of phase transitions in human hand movements | Haken, Kelso & Bunz (1985), Biological Cybernetics 51(5):347–356. The HKB model, as described by Kelso 2021 ([LIT-601](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-601.md)): relative phase φ between two rhythmically moving fingers is the order parameter, with potential V(φ) = −a cos φ − b cos 2φ; anti-phase coordination loses stability as movement frequency rises and the hands switch to in-phase, and the φ dynamics is derived from two nonlinearly coupled oscillators. Unread: registered from metadata and a secondary account. | Deferred — registered 2026-10-03, not read. No lawful full text was found. Unpaywall lists the article as closed; Springer's page offers it only by subscription or purchase; Europe PMC has the record (PMID 3978150) without full text; no author or repository deposit turned up in a web search. The read substitute is Kelso's 2021 retrospective on the model ([LIT-601](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-601.md)), which gives the model's equations and regimes. A reader with Springer access could read the ten pages and promote this. |
| [LIT-591](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-591.md) | Internal Family Systems Therapy | Schwartz & Sweezy (2019/2020), Guilford, 2nd ed., the authoritative text of Internal Family Systems therapy. IFS synthesises "the plural mind, or the idea that we all contain many different parts, and systems thinking". Extreme parts are protectors or burdened exiles, not pathology, and everyone has a Self that can lead the inner system once parts "step back". Therapy restores trust in the Self's leadership and unburdens exiles. Chapter 1 read; the rest unread. | Deferred — chapter 1 read in full 2026-10-03 ([NOTE-457](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-457.md), Skimmed), from the sample chapter Guilford posts; the other nineteen chapters unread. Per the report's ERIC abstract: routine action runs off by "contention scheduling" among competing schemas, and a "supervisory attentional mechanism" biases that selection for novel, ill-learned, dangerous or planned action; "will becomes the application of attentional resources to the control of action". | [LIT-601](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-601.md) | The Haken–Kelso–Bunz (HKB) model: from matter to movement to mind | Kelso (2021), Biological Cybernetics 115(4):305–322, a 60th-anniversary retrospective. HKB models bimanual coordination by the relative phase φ, with dφ/dt = −a sin φ − 2b sin 2φ and potential V = −a cos φ − b cos 2φ: both in-phase and anti-phase are stable for b/a > 1/4, and anti-phase loses stability below it, as observed when movement frequency rises. Noise, symmetry breaking (Δω) and metastability extend it; with Kuramoto's model it becomes a generalized HKB for many agents. The same dynamics is reported within a body, between people and with machines, and in brain activity. | Active — read in full 2026-10-03 ([NOTE-467](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-467.md)), from the free-to-read publisher PDF. Filed in place of Kelso's book Dynamic Patterns ([LIT-578](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-578.md)) and as the read account of the paywalled Haken–Kelso–Bunz paper ([LIT-588](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-588.md)), both Deferred. Worth reading as Kelso's own short statement of coordination dynamics: the HKB order-parameter equation for relative phase, its stochastic and symmetry-breaking extensions, metastability as relative coordination, the generalized HKB–Kuramoto model, and the claim that one coordination dynamics holds within and between people. It is a retrospective by an author of the model, not a review, and it says so. |
| [LIT-602](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-602.md) | The Intimate Contest for Self-Command | Schelling (1980), The Public Interest, Summer 1980, pp. 94-118. People behave sometimes "as if they had two selves" in "continual contest for control", and the tactics of self-management (removing the option, bright lines, monitoring, delays, raising the stakes) are the tactics of managing someone else. A single-dimension model of impatience fits poorly. Which self is authentic is left open. Failures of consumer self-management may be worth "on the order of a trillion dollars". | Active — read in full 2026-10-03 ([NOTE-452](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-452.md)), in place of the 1984 Ely Lecture ([LIT-573](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-573.md)), which has no lawful free copy. Worth reading as Schelling's own first statement of "egonomics": a person sometimes behaves "as if they had two selves" that alternate in command, and the tactics people use on themselves (mittens, alarm clocks across the room, bright lines, Christmas savings, deadlines, delays) are the tactics they use to manage another person. It refuses to say which self is authentic in general, and it gives an order-of-magnitude estimate that failures of consumer self-management cost as much as all other consumer-ignorance problems together. |

| [LIT-605](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-605.md) | An Accumulator Model for Spontaneous Neural Activity Prior to Self-Initiated Movement | Schurger, Sitt & Dehaene (2012), PNAS 109(42). In Libet's spontaneous movement task, a leaky stochastic accumulator, δx = (I − kx)Δt + cξ√Δt, with weak constant urgency I and a threshold, fitted only to waiting times, reproduces the averaged readiness potential (r² = 0.96): time-locking to threshold crossings averages up the autocorrelated noise that produced them. Fast responses to random interruptions were preceded by a slow negativity, as predicted. The "neural decision to move now" is the late threshold crossing, about 150 ms before movement, so Libet's inference of an unconscious decision a half-second earlier is unfounded. | Active — read in full 2026-10-03 ([NOTE-462](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-462.md)); worth reading as the model that reinterprets the readiness potential. A leaky stochastic accumulator with a weak constant input ("urgency"), fitted with three parameters to 14 participants' waiting times in Libet's task, reproduces the shape of the averaged readiness potential (r² = 0.96) because averaging epochs time-locked to threshold crossings recovers the noise that happened to carry the accumulator there. Its prediction, that fast responses to unpredictable clicks are preceded by a slow negativity, was confirmed (13 participants). On this account the "neural decision to move now" is the threshold crossing about 150 ms before movement, not the onset of the readiness potential, and Libet's inference that the brain decides before awareness is "unfounded". The authors say plainly that this shows the readiness potential could reflect spontaneous fluctuation, not that it does. |
